To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the quality of products, their diffusion, and incremental and radical innovation depend on the degree of complementarity of the competencies of the firms involved, and on the degree of trust and relational governance.
the quality of innovation and the diffusion of innovation depend on the mix of governance instruments.
trust and opportunism are not opposites but complementary.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how firms can best organize their relationships with other firms.
how firms and other organizations can be organized in such a way that the potential benefits of innovation can be realized.
the role of trust in innovation and the governance of inter firm linkages.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a mix of instruments for governance of inter firm linkages, including trust, is needed.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the European and Japanese systems are more effective in producing high quality products, and the Anglo-American ones are more effective in diffusion and radical innovation.

the article shows how the theory of transactions can be transformed into a theory of learning and innovation, and how this can be used for the analysis and design of inter firm linkages, and for the evaluation and redesign of generic systems of innovation and government policy.

the article discusses the implications of different modes of governance for the quality of products, the rate and direction of diffusion of innovations, the rate of incremental innovation, and the rate of radical innovation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no one best way, but that different systems have different merits and flaws, and that the choice between systems is not only a matter of efficiency, but also of politics.
trust is a key element of innovation and learning, but it is not enough.
the choice of instruments for governance is not just a matter of transaction cost reduction.
